messages:
customer-acct: Hey, hitting a burst of 429s on rwd-large when we submit ~10k token contexts. Only happens under spikes — sustained 20rpm is fine but short fanouts cause rejects. Not seeing auth issues. Any quick mitigation?
ben-support: Sorry about that — can you paste a sample request id or a curl snippet? Also approximate concurrency when spikes happen?
customer-acct: No request ids yet, here's a minimal repro curl we used: 
```\
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ACCT' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large","input":"<10k_tokens_here>","max_tokens":1024}'\
```
We ramp 30 parallel requests for a short window (10s) then drop. Observed a lot of 429s with body: "rate limit exceeded: per-model concurrency or burst".
alice-cs: Thanks — are you doing any prefetch/fanout or parallelizing on the client side? 30 parallel > default concurrency. Can you try linearizing to 5 concurrent and see if it improves?
customer-acct: It's a mix — client uses 1 worker per user, spikes during onboarding lead to bursts. We can throttle on client but would like to understand server limits so we can set client-side backoff correctly.
maria-sre: Jumping in — 429s usually due to per-model request rate (RPM/TPM) or max concurrency. For rwd-large the soft concurrency target for hosted tenants is 8 concurrent infer requests/model per key; longer context increases compute per request so queueing can push into 429s.
ben-support: Can you share X-Request-Id header from next failure? That helps trace in logs, but in the meantime try reducing parallelism to 6-8 and add exponential backoff + jitter.
customer-acct: Ok we'll test that. Curious about exact values: what's rpm/tpm vs concurrency?
darren-ml: Quick note from model side — rwd-large has a tighter TPM cap for very-long contexts because token accounting multiplies by (context_length + generated_tokens). Example limits: ~120 RPM and ~600k TPM on hosted; max concurrent infer ops ~8. These are per-model *and* per-API-key. Bursts are accepted only if within burst window; long contexts consume burst budget quickly.
maria-sre: Also watch for preflight/prefetch patterns — if you fan out one long-context request into many model requests (e.g., embedding prefetch + generation) you amplify token consumption.
customer-acct: Hmm ok. If we can't refactor client fast, any immediate server-side options?
ben-support: Short term: (1) switch to rwd-large-quant or rwd-medium for heavy fanouts, (2) enable streaming where possible to reduce end-to-end RTTs, (3) request a temporary quota bump via support if you have predictable windows. I can open a ticket to request a short burst raise.
billing-bot: Note: quota or plan changes may impact billing. Any temporary bump will be tied to a usage review.
customer-acct: Please open the ticket — we have a marketing push next week.
ben-support: Done — ticket #SUP-8742 created, adding eng and SRE. Please add example trace ids when you see more 429s.
deploy-bot: alert: noticed request-id traces for api-key sk-ACCT in last 15m with 429 spikes (see /internal/traces/1766504321-8742).
maria-sre: I'm pulling logs now. If you can run a controlled repro that we can watch, run this script (runs 10->30 concurrent ramp): 
```\n# simple repro (do not run in prod)\nfor c in 5 10 20 30; do\n  seq 1 $c | xargs -n1 -P$c -I{} curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{url_effective}\n" \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ACCT' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-large","input":"<10k>","max_tokens":64}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate ;\n  sleep 10;\ndone\n```
We'll tail logs while you run that.
customer-acct: Running now, sending first batch.
ben-support: Received first trace batch. I'm seeing 429s start when concurrency hits ~16; the throttles mention both "per-model concurrency" and "burst window".
darren-ml: Confirmed — when context >8k tokens rwd-large uses more GPU memory and we reduce allowable concurrent slots dynamically to protect SLOs. That dynamic QoS shows as 429s rather than slow responses.
customer-acct: Is this expected behavior? It caught us off guard.
maria-sre: It's intentional to avoid cascading latency tail. Short-term options: reduce client concurrency, use a model variant with higher concurrency limits (rwd-large-batch or quant), or request dedicated capacity (Redwood Dedicated) to guarantee throughput. Long-term we'll improve error messaging to indicate which limit (RPM/TPM/concurrency) triggered the 429.
ben-support: I've added recommended client retry header pattern to the ticket and a sample backoff: Retry-After with exponential base 1.5 + jitter, cap 60s.
customer-acct: Appreciate the guidance. One last ask — how to programmatically detect which limit hit so we can auto-fallback?
darren-ml: Current best practice: inspect 429 body for fields "limit_type" (request|token|concurrency) and X-RateLimit-* headers if present. If limit_type=="concurrency" fallback to smaller model or queue. If "token" or "tpm" reduce context or delay requests. We're tracking a small enhancement to standardize those fields.
customer-acct: Great, will implement. Thanks everyone.
ben-support: Leaving follow-up items in the ticket: reproduce traces, potential quota bump, client backoff guidance, and recommended model variants. Will loop back after SRE confirms logs. :thumbsup:
